summary: Erratic 5xx pulses during slow-client keepalive bursts causing API gateway accept-queue collapse
description: Issue summary: Multiple customers (largest: StreamlineAI) reported short-lived waves of 5xx responses on streaming and embedding endpoints. Impact: customer requests during bursts receive 502/503/504 with high variance in first-byte times; some long-lived streaming sessions drop mid-stream. Environment: prod us-east serving dedicated fleet for StreamlineAI (reserved capacity). Observed pattern: errors occur in short pulses lasting ~30-120s, often in evenings, correlated with a small subset of upstream runtimes cycling and API gateway accept-queue growth.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run sustained mixed traffic: many long-lived streaming connections (keepalive HTTP/2) interspersed with embedding upload batches from a small client pool.
2) Introduce a client behavior that sends delayed window updates and occasional tiny payload bursts (simulates slow consumer with sporadic writes).
3) Observe apigw accept-queue length and backend handshake times; monitor for 5xx pulses on edge and runtime restarts.
logs: Mar 10 18:21:35 runtime-ephemeral-12: SIGTERM triggered due to watchdog timeout during prefetched-model lock (nvml reset)
Mar 10 18:22:01 apigw-44ab proxy: upstream 10.0.12.8 reset while reading response header (502)
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Pattern suggests accept-queue growth at apigw followed by short upstream restarts (watchdog timeouts) rather than a single sustained overload.
SRE observation: CPU on apigw hosts spikes concurrently with keepalive churn; fd usage climbs but not full exhaustion. Accept queue length correlates with 5xx pulse start times.
Runtime logs: One runtime process hit a GPU driver reset and triggered a local restart; subsequent reshuffling of ephemeral workers increased connection handoffs.

Hypothesis 1: Slow-client windowing causes partial reads at the proxy, leaving sockets tied up and causing accept-queue pressure; when accept queue backpressure increases, the apigw amplifies retries to upstreams causing transient overload and runtime watchdog timeouts.

Hypothesis 2: Small number of long-lived streaming sessions from StreamlineAI are unevenly distributed across apigw nodes; when a node experiences runtime restart, the rebalancing amplifies ephemeral load onto neighbors, creating a short 5xx pulse.

Observed mitigations tried: temporarily shifting customer route weight off the hot apigw hosts decreased pulse frequency; adding a short client-side keepalive threshold on StreamlineAI reduced connection churn in testing.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reports 5xx pulses ~18:20-18:25 local time yesterday. They provided a sample timeseries and a pcap of a single streaming session (attached to ticket). Asked SRE for initial log sweep.

SRE (Diego): Pulled apigw host metrics and runtime logs. Found accept_queue spikes and a runtime GPU reset on runtime-12. Suspect prefetched model lock contention contributed to watchdog timeouts. Investigating fd leak hypothesis.

Eng (Marta Novak): Noted a recent ingress-proxy tweak (PR #7891) changed the read timeout semantics for half-closed streams. Will review if this increased partial-read retention. Linking PR: github.com/redwood/pr/7891

Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed they perform periodic tiny writes from an SDK under poor network conditions (mobile). They can try increasing their client-side keepalive frequency for a test window.

SRE (Diego): Scoped mitigation: increased apigw accept-queue cap on the affected AZ and temporarily diverted 30% of StreamlineAI traffic to a healthy pod group (route weight change). Monitoring for recurrence.
Eng (Ethan Shaw): Adding a short-term circuit in the ingress to penalize connections that emit long tail windowing behavior. Drafting patch (WIP) and load test plan.
resolution_notes: Workaround: shifted StreamlineAI route weights away from three saturated apigw nodes and applied a temporary ingress policy to drop half-closed idle streams after 45s. Customer applied a conservative SDK keepalive fix during the window. Result: 5xx pulses frequency dropped to zero during the monitoring window. Next steps: eng to land ingress PR to tighten partial-read retention and backpressure handling; SRE to add alerting threshold for accept-queue growth and autopurge policy. Postmortem scheduled.
